title: Supabase Small Examples
description: Use these small Supabase examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Know the database and the client
examples.description: Supabase stores table data in PostgreSQL and exposes APIs around it.
examples.code:
Browser page -> Supabase API -> PostgreSQL table
The public client key identifies the project.
Row-level security decides which rows the client role may access.
examples.output: The worked flow separates the browser request from the database permission check.

examples.title: Create a local sample table
examples.description: A PostgreSQL table defines the fields used by the API.
examples.code: CREATE TABLE public.cma_books(id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,title text NOT NULL,pages integer CHECK(pages>0));
examples.output: The local database has an empty sample table for books.

examples.title: Seed public sample records
examples.description: Seed data is a small set of known records used for learning or testing.
examples.code: INSERT INTO public.cma_books(title,pages) VALUES('Moon Trip',60),('Garden Days',40),('Tiny Seed',20);
examples.output: The three sample records are inserted through the local database tool.

examples.title: Enable row-level security
examples.description: Row-level security adds a database check for rows accessed through client roles.
examples.code: ALTER TABLE public.cma_books ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
examples.output: The table now uses row-level security. The public client still needs an explicit read policy.

examples.title: Allow only the public read
examples.description: A SELECT policy can make fictional sample rows readable to the anon role.
examples.code:
GRANT SELECT ON public.cma_books TO anon;
CREATE POLICY "Read public sample books" ON public.cma_books FOR SELECT TO anon USING (true);
examples.output: The anon client can read these public sample books. This policy does not grant insert, update or delete access.

examples.title: Make a local client
examples.description: createClient connects the JavaScript SDK to the chosen project API.
examples.output: After replacing the placeholder with the local public key from supabase status, the client can make permitted requests.

examples.title: Select named columns
examples.description: A select request can ask only for the columns a page needs.
examples.output: With the table and policy ready, the result contains the sample ids and titles.

examples.title: Filter with a comparison
examples.description: The client can add a filter to a query. gte means greater than or equal to.
examples.output: The sample result includes Moon Trip with 60 pages.

examples.title: Order and limit the result
examples.description: Ordering and limiting help a page request a small useful set.
examples.output: Tiny Seed and Garden Days are the two shortest sample books.

examples.title: Count without requesting every row
examples.description: A select can request a count while leaving the row body out.
examples.output: The count is 3 for the seeded sample table visible to this role.

examples.title: Expect a denied write
examples.description: A read-only policy should reject browser writes.
examples.output: With only the read permissions from this course, the insert is denied.

examples.title: Keep environments separate
examples.description: Local and hosted projects have different addresses and keys.
examples.code:
Local development: local URL, local public key, fictional sample rows.
Hosted app: its own public URL/key and reviewed policies.
Server-only operations: secret key kept out of browser bundles.
Before running changes: verify which project the client points to.
examples.output: The worked checklist keeps the practice project and a real app from being confused.
